pr_body:
It also gives suggestions for valid arguments.

Fix: https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/12338

issue_context.title: Issue with Python duckdb.read_csv not working with 0.10.2+
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

Reading from a StringIO buffer works in 0.10.1, but not in 0.10.2 or 0.10.3.

### To Reproduce

download the csv files from:

* https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/3xpwlfgfc0seoe4lw3vwk/cad_fi_cp1252.csv?rlkey=2wanizbvs6nr7tzrgwvquj6mf&dl=1
* https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/anbvm5n9gpp0dgxfanipp/cad_fi_utf8.csv?rlkey=mxdqw3disqn12lqb4d88j6woo&dl=1

and run the following script:

from io import StringIO

import duckdb


def load_csv(filename, encoding, newline="\r\n"):
    with open(filename, "rb") as fp:
        content = fp.read().decode(encoding)
        _buffer = StringIO(content.replace(newline, "\n"), newline="\n")
        return duckdb.read_csv(
            _buffer,
            normalize_names=True,
            sample_size=-1,
        )


cad_fi_utf8 = load_csv("cad_fi_utf8.csv", "utf-8")
cad_fi_cp1252 = load_csv("cad_fi_cp1252.csv", "cp1252")

assert (
    duckdb.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM cad_fi_utf8").fetchone()
    == duckdb.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM cad_fi_cp1252").fetchone()
), "Different number of rows"


### OS:

Windows 11

### DuckDB Version:

0.10.3

### DuckDB Client:

0.10.3

### Full Name:

Leo Horta

### Affiliation:

Sparta Fundos de Investimento

### What is the latest build you tested with? If possible, we recommend testing with the latest nightly build.

I have tested with a stable release

### Did you include all relevant data sets for reproducing the issue?

Yes

### Did you include all code required to reproduce the issue?

- [X] Yes, I have

### Did you include all relevant configuration (e.g., CPU architecture, Python version, Linux distribution) to reproduce the issue?

- [X] Yes, I have

Opa Leonardo, tudo bem? :-)

I tested the  
```sql
select count(*) from read_csv('cad_fi_utf8.csv', sample_size=-1)
```
and it seems to work fine.

Notice that 
```sql
select count(*) from read_csv('cad_fi_utf8.csv')
```
will fail because the sniffer only sniffs the first 20480 lines, and it will not detect that " should not be a quoted option.

You can tell that from the line 
`FI;37.267.399/0001-81;SANTANDER PB ALOCAÇÃO AÇÕES LONG ONLY FIC FI;2020-10-27;2020-04-30;381373;;EM FUNCIONAMENTO NORMAL;2020-10-29;2020-10-29;2024-01-01;2024-12-31;Fundo de Ações;2020-04-30;Índice de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA/IBGE);Aberto;S;N;;Qualificado;;10;"1" é calculado de acordo com a seguinte fórmula: média ponderada, calculada diariamente, das taxas indicativas dos títulos que compõem o índice IMA-B de acordo com o peso dos títulos na composição do próprio índice, de acordo com as taxas diárias divulgadas pela ANBIMA - Associação Brasileira das Entidades dos Mercados Financeiro e de Capitais, em seu website.;1;;72689801.68;2024-05-28;ALESSANDRO CHAGAS FARIAS;03.502.968/0001-04;SANTANDER DISTRIBUIDORA DE TÍTULOS E VALORES MOBILIÁRIOS S.A.;PJ;03.502.968/0001-04;SANTANDER DISTRIBUIDORA DE TÍTULOS E VALORES MOBILIÁRIOS S.A.;61.366.936/0001-25;ERNST & YOUNG AUDITORES INDEPENDENTES S/S LTDA.;62.318.407/0001-19;S3 CACEIS BRASIL DISTRIBUIDORA DE TITULOS E VALORES MOBILIARIOS S.A;62.318.407/0001-19;S3 CACEIS BRASIL DISTRIBUIDORA DE TITULOS E VALORES MOBILIARIOS S.A;N;Ações Livre`
the value
`"1" é calculado de acordo com a seguinte fórmula: média ponderada, calculada diariamente, das taxas indicativas dos títulos que compõem o índice IMA-B de acordo com o peso dos títulos na composição do próprio índice, de acordo com as taxas diárias divulgadas pela ANBIMA - Associação Brasileira das Entidades dos Mercados Financeiro e de Capitais, em seu website.` is poorly quoted.

Another option is to instead of setting the sample size to -1, you can also set it the quote value to something other than `"`.
e.g.,
`select count(*) from read_csv('cad_fi_utf8.csv', quote='')`

I ran these based in feature, so please try them out on a feature build and let me know if it works or if you still have any questions!

I've noticed a difference in the `sniff_csv` function's behavior. In DuckDB version 0.10.1, the escape and quote characters are determined as `\0` with the default sample size. However, in version 0.10.3 and later, they are correctly identified as `"`. It seems there was a bug in the earlier version that left the escape and quote characters as `\0`, which inadvertently solved my parsing error by ignoring poorly quoted fields. When this bug was fixed, it broke my application.

Now, there's seems to be another issue in the Python API: I can't override the quote and escape characters to correctly parse my poorly quoted CSV file.
Anyone observed this commentary: "I can't override the quote and escape characters to correctly parse my poorly quoted CSV file."
